evals.prompt: I'm building a delivery app on the Mapbox Standard style. I added a choropleth of delivery zones, the driver's active route line, and pin markers for the stops — but all three are drawing on top of the street labels, and the route disappears when the map switches to the night preset. Why is this happening, and how do I place these three correctly?
evals.expected_output: Should place layers with `slot`, not `beforeId` and not by hand-ordering the basemap: choropleth in `middle` (or `bottom` if it should sit under roads), route in `middle`, markers in `top`. Should state that an unslotted layer's position isn't something to rely on — above every layer in non-globe projections, below labels under `globe` — so every custom layer needs an explicit slot. Should require fill-emissive-strength / line-emissive-strength: 1 on all three, and line-occlusion-opacity on the route so 3D buildings don't hide it.
expectations: Uses the `slot` property rather than `beforeId` or a hand-ordered layer stack
Puts the route line in `middle`, not `top`
Puts the marker/symbol layer in `top`
Warns that an unslotted layer's placement is projection-dependent and must not be relied on — set a slot explicitly
Requires fill-emissive-strength / line-emissive-strength of 1 on the custom layers
Mentions line-occlusion-opacity for the route under 3D buildings

evals.prompt: Our app has a dark theme and the map needs to follow it. I already set colorLand to #12181f and colorRoads to #2a3f5a plus lightPreset night, and now the map is basically solid black. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should identify the double-darkening failure: Standard interprets every color* override as its day appearance and re-derives it for the active preset, so a night-tuned colorLand gets darkened again under `night`. Fix is to author the overrides as day values (or drop them and let the preset do the work) — lightPreset:'night' alone gives a real dark basemap. Should also note that the developer's own custom layers do NOT adapt and need emissive strength, and should not suggest CSS invert() or a hand-built parallel night palette.
expectations: Identifies that config color overrides are day values that Standard re-derives per light preset
States that supplying already-dark colors plus lightPreset night double-darkens to near-black
Says lightPreset:'night' on its own produces a legitimate dark basemap
Notes that custom layers do not adapt and need fill-/line-emissive-strength: 1
Does not recommend CSS invert() or inverting the rendered map
Recommends binding the preset to the OS/UI appearance signal rather than a separate style

evals.prompt: I'm putting a county-level population-density choropleth on a Mapbox map. Which basemap setup should I use, what color ramp, and what opacity?
evals.expected_output: Should pick a quiet base: theme 'monochrome' (or 'faded'), or the purpose-built light-2d / dark-2d styles; POI labels off and 3D off, because POIs compete with the thematic layer and 3D occludes it. Should choose a sequential ColorBrewer ramp (Blues, Greens, Oranges, YlOrRd, BuPu) and explicitly reject rainbow/spectral for ordered data. Should cap fill-opacity at 0.7 so the road network still reads through, and place the fill in a slot (middle, or bottom to sit under roads) with fill-emissive-strength 1.
expectations: Recommends theme 'monochrome' or 'faded' (or the light-2d / dark-2d styles) rather than the default basemap
Turns off POI labels and 3D objects
Chooses a sequential ColorBrewer ramp and names at least one
Explicitly rejects rainbow/spectral ramps for ordered data
Caps fill-opacity at or below 0.7
Assigns an explicit slot to the choropleth fill layer

evals.prompt: We render a PNG of our map server-side for an emailed weekly report, and our fintech client wants their brand purple in it. I'll be hand-authoring the style JSON — which style should I base it on, what order do I stack the layers in, and where should the brand purple actually be applied?
evals.expected_output: Should say the Static Images API cannot render Standard, so the PNG needs a Classic style (streets-v12, light-v11, dark-v11, outdoors-v12, satellite-v9, satellite-streets-v12) where you author the layer stack yourself — bottom to top: background, land use, water, terrain, buildings, roads, borders, labels, POI symbols, user content. Should say brand color belongs on user content only — routes, markers, pins — and never on basemap roads, water, or land, and should name that as the most common map-design mistake.
expectations: States that Standard cannot be rendered by the Static Images API and a Classic style is required
Names at least one Classic style id
Gives the bottom-to-top layer order with user content on top for the hand-authored Classic style
Puts brand color on routes, markers, and pins only
Explicitly rules out brand color on basemap roads, water, or land
